parsed.explanation: The division itself carries no documented universal exposure: no facility ban, no sex-definition law, no criminalised presentation, repeated gubernatorial vetoes of care and sports bans, an executive order barring gender-identity discrimination in state services, and a July 2026 assessment placing it in the low-risk group. These are territory-specific mitigations. But the parent regime still binds: visa adjudication instructions to refuse cases where documents cast doubt on sex, the X-marker ban, allied travel advisories, airport screening outing risk, and birth-sex federal custody including the 2026 conversion-therapy-style corrections policy. Recourse is thin locally: no statewide gender-identity nondiscrimination law and no gender identity in the state hate-crime statute (sexual orientation is used as a proxy). So: protective local climate and institutions, but an operative hostile document/entry and custody layer inherited from the parent, with incomplete remedy.
